sources.citation: Berglund, Darcy (Ethnos360/NTM). 2019. ISO 639-3 Change Request 2019-043 (split of sdm Semandang into Semandang sdq, Beginci ebc, Gerai gef) and New Code Request form for sdq Semandang/Kualan. SIL ISO 639-3 Registration Authority.
sources.note: Nothing. States that 'distinct phonemic write-ups' of Semandang, Gerai and Beginci by NTM linguists exist and were attached to the request (not posted online); lists Semandang dialects (Kualan, Sajan, Komi, Entuka', Tontang, Kasiau, Kukot, Banyor, Koman, Kembera, Daramán).

sources.citation: Smith, Alexander D. 2017. The Languages of Borneo: A Comprehensive Classification. PhD dissertation, University of Hawai'i at Manoa.

sources.note: Lists a 'Simpang' Land Dayak wordlist (Kampar Sembomban) used for subgrouping only; no stress statement for it.

sources.citation: Rensch, Calvin R., Carolyn M. Rensch, Jonas Noeb & Robert Sulis Ridu. 2012. The Bidayuh Language: Yesterday, Today and Tomorrow (rev. ed.). SIL e-Books 33.
sources.note: States final (ultima) word stress for Sarawak Bidayuh (different glottocodes); its Semandang material is only Hudson 1970 wordlist items used in Proto Land Dayak sets — no prosodic statement about Semandang.

sources.citation: [Brad], MPI-EVA Jakarta Field Station. ca. 2010. 'Semandang & co.: Semandang, Kualan, Baram (A Land Dayak Language)'. 9-slide internal presentation (lingweb.eva.mpg.de/jakarta/docs/, via the Internet Archive).
sources.note: Nothing; the 'Phonemic inventory' slide only notes glides, 'preploded nasals', and refers to an offline consonant_inventory.xls.

sources.citation: Tadmor, Uri. 2009. Developing an orthography for Onya Darat (western Borneo): Practical and theoretical considerations. Wacana, Journal of the Humanities of Indonesia 11(2): 279-293. doi:10.17510/wjhi.v11i2.162
sources.note: Nothing on stress placement. Sec. 5-6 (pp. 282-284) give the Kualan-dialect segment inventory (5 vowels, 19 simple consonants, prenasalized stops, preoralized and postoralized nasals); the only occurrence of 'stress' is the generic remark (p. 280) that an orthography should represent phonemic contrasts 'whether segmental (consonants, vowels) or suprasegmental (tone, stress)'.

sources.citation: Tadmor, Uri. 2004/2007. 'Kualan and Samandang' project page, MPI-EVA Jakarta Field Station (Internet Archive copy 2007-06-10).
sources.note: Nothing; sociolinguistic project blurb (Malay contact, object-focus infix, classifiers).

sources.note: NTM phonemic statements routinely state stress placement; Semandang write-up is by long-resident fieldworkers (1992-2017). Obtainable from the ISO 639-3 registrar or Ethnos360 (darcy_berglund at ntm dot org).
